why_it_matters: SOFR is the cornerstone reference rate for US money markets and affects the pricing of derivatives, floating-rate loans, and securitization products. Even small changes in SOFR signal shifts in bank funding conditions and the broader cost of short-term capital. Market participants use SOFR levels to gauge stress in the secured funding market and to price interest rate swaps and Eurodollar futures.
market_structure_context: SOFR is produced by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York using overnight repo transactions secured by Treasury securities. It replaced LIBOR as the primary reference rate for dollar markets. The current 3.64% level reflects normal money market conditions with no indication of stress. The narrow recent range (3.63-3.67%) suggests stable collateral availability and balanced supply/demand in the overnight repo market.
